clue.text: Dribble puts ball at last within grasp of competent goalie?

indicators.note: the goalie's hands close around the letter, so it sits inside his word

parts.note: a competent goalkeeper is a good saver of shots

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word ball is wanted here

explanation.surface: A football commentator wonders whether a capable keeper will hold a dribbled shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dribble' looks like football, but it is the definition: to slaver is to let saliva run. 'at last' takes L from 'ball'; 'within grasp of' puts it inside SAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to drool, letting spit run from the mouth.

clue.text: Girl gets acceptance from French department in London college

indicators.note: the French yes is placed inside the letters of the college

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics, a college of London University
oui is French for yes, a word of acceptance

explanation.surface: A young woman is accepted by a French department at a London college.
explanation.walkthrough: The London School of Economics is a London University college. 'department' only dresses the surface: a French department at a college suggests a languages course.
explanation.definitionFit: Louise is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Way to consume beer and regular amounts of nice port

indicators.note: the route word swallows the other letters, holding them inside itself

parts.note: via means by way of, a route
ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word nice, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A traveller's route includes beer and modest amounts of pleasant wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine, but it is a harbour city. 'regular amounts of' takes N and C from 'nice'; 'to consume' puts ALENC inside VIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a major Spanish seaport on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Preparation for exam? That mates a change!

definitions.meaning: studying notes again before a test, in British usage
the act of making an alteration to a text or plan

explanation.walkthrough: The page as read says 'mates'; the setter wrote 'makes', so the second half is the exclamation 'That makes a change!' read literally as an alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, students do revision when they reread course work before an exam; an amendment to a document is also called this.

clue.text: Thieves reportedly needed briefs

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word for thieves is heard rather than read

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal, so nickers are thieves

explanation.surface: It is said the robbers wanted some short documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefs' suggests legal papers, but it is underwear. NICK is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's underpants, and briefs are close-fitting underpants.

clue.text: Foreign dog food, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the words for dog food are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a cur is a dog and a dish is food, so a cur dish

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a meal for a dog is imported from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurdish describes the Kurds of the Middle East, so it is foreign to a British reader.

clue.text: Drug obtained from prison one's placed under arrest

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters below come later, so this piece follows

parts.note: can is American slang for jail
to nab is to arrest
one is I, and 's stands for is, giving I'S

explanation.surface: A narcotic is seized in jail when an inmate is arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is a psychoactive plant product, smoked or eaten as a narcotic.

clue.text: Emergency: English team on dope caught with ecstasy

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football side
gen is British slang for information, like dope
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A crisis as an English side is found taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like a drug, but here it means inside information, GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigence is an urgent need or pressing demand, a crisis requiring action.

clue.text: Old ship arrives in Tasmania unexpectedly

indicators.note: something arriving out of the blue is disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: AR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: A historic vessel turns up off the Australian island without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' shuffles AR with TASMANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Santa Maria was the flagship of Columbus on his 1492 voyage.

clue.text: Jersey traffic cop's order to offending motorist?

definitions.meaning: a knitted woollen top worn over the upper body

definitions.text: traffic cop's order to offending motorist?
definitions.meaning: an instruction to stop the car at the roadside

explanation.definitionFit: A pullover is a sweater, and a police officer tells a driver to pull over and stop.

clue.text: In bed, not very brave

indicators.note: the letter for very is left out of the furniture word

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed

explanation.surface: Someone lying in bed is not particularly courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, an old term for such a fighter.

clue.text: American flicks kept from the public?

indicators.note: a flick jerks things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Hollywood films are kept under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flicks' looks like films, but it is the signal to shuffle AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal phrase for proceedings held in private, closed to outsiders.

clue.text: Backward set mostly longing to enrol in special classes?

indicators.note: the yearning word joins the group, going inside its letters
the word set is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of the longing word is dropped

parts.note: aching means longing

explanation.surface: A slow group of pupils, keen to sign up for extra lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: A backward set is a slow class of pupils, which makes 'Backward' look like an adjective; it is the reversal signal. 'mostly' drops the last letter; 'to enrol in' places one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Teach-ins are informal sessions of lectures and debate on a topic, so unusual lessons.

clue.text: MOT cheater fixed this?

indicators.note: rigging something alters it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest motorist tampered with a dashboard gauge to pass his vehicle test.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars. 'fixed' shuffles MOT CHEATER, and the whole clue describes a gauge a cheat might tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A tachometer is a dial measuring engine revolutions, the sort of instrument a cheat might rig.

clue.text: Artist from Penzance needing no introduction, oddly

indicators.note: the remaining letters are placed in a strange new order
the first letter of the town is dropped

explanation.surface: A painter from a Cornish town is so famous he needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a town in Cornwall. 'needing no introduction' drops P to leave ENZANCE; 'oddly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Cézanne was a French Post-Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Legion succeeded after misfortune in Israel

indicators.note: this abbreviation comes last, following the rest
the bad luck word goes inside the name for the land

parts.note: Zion is a poetic name for Israel
an ill is a misfortune
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A Roman legion triumphed after trouble in the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legion' looks like a Roman army unit, but means a huge number.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as a noun means a vast multitude, a countless quantity.

clue.text: Source of information all about the uplands and the great city

indicators.note: both pieces are turned around together, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: moors are high open uplands
the Great Wen is an old nickname for London

explanation.surface: A guidebook covering the highlands and London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all about' turns MOORSWEN to NEWSROOM. William Cobbett called London 'the Great Wen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsroom is where reporters gather and edit stories, so it supplies news.

clue.text: Who might provide a service on back street of Pigalle?

definitions.text: Who might provide a service on back street of Pigalle?

parts.note: mass is a church service

indicators.note: the street word is read backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street, and Pigalle is a Paris district

explanation.surface: A Paris red-light district hint: who offers services on a side street of Pigalle?
explanation.walkthrough: Pigalle is a Paris district known for nightlife, which makes 'service' look seedy. 'back' turns RUE to EUR. The whole clue describes one who rubs backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur is a man who gives massages, often working on clients' backs.

clue.text: What's the going rate for a Jumbo?

definitions.text: What's the going rate for a Jumbo?

parts.words: What's the going rate for a Jumbo?
parts.note: 'going rate' reads as a price, but means how fast a jumbo jet travels through the air

explanation.definitionFit: Airspeed is the velocity of an aircraft relative to the surrounding air, the speed a jet flies at.

clue.text: Safely deposited former European currency in second bank

indicators.note: money paid in is placed somewhere, so these letters are set within
the currency letters sit inside the other two pieces

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
the ecu was the European currency unit before the euro

explanation.surface: Old European money was safely paid into another bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a financial institution, which fits 'deposited', but here it is the verb as in 'bank on'. The ecu preceded the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Securely means in a protected way, free from danger.

clue.text: Pin-up grabbed by macho Roman soldiers

indicators.note: the macho word seizes the other, holding it inside

parts.note: macho means manly, male

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word pin is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A glamour poster is snatched by a he-man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin-up' looks like a poster, but it is PIN plus 'up', which turns it to NIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniple was a subdivision of a Roman legion, a company of soldiers.

clue.text: Roman general, one meeting officer in Mogul capital

indicators.note: the number and the rank go inside the city name

parts.note: Agra was the capital of the Mughal empire
I is one in Roman numerals
Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A Roman commander meets an officer in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agricola was a Roman governor of Britain, famed for military campaigns.

clue.text: The work of art is in French, not English museum

indicators.note: the abbreviation for English is left out of the French phrase

parts.words: The work of art is in French
parts.note: l'oeuvre is French for the work

explanation.surface: This masterpiece is in a French museum rather than an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'museum' seems to belong with 'English', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre is the great Paris art gallery, home of the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Spy's relatives hide

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted in an organisation, and the 's gives MOLE'S
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: The family of an agent go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Moleskin is the fur of a mole, or a heavy cotton fabric resembling it.

clue.text: Excessively affected by announcement of score draw

indicators.note: a football result is read out, so the score is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a two-two result is a draw with goals

explanation.surface: A football pundit overreacts when a high-scoring tie is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: A score draw is British football-pools language for a tied match with goals scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Too-too means overdone or precious in manner, an old slang word for affected.

clue.text: Result of jam session, with extra player on piano

indicators.note: the substitute follows the musical letter, placed on it

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
a reserve is a substitute player

explanation.surface: A jazz jam session, with a stand-in musician on keyboards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam session' looks like music, but means making jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserve is fruit cooked with sugar and stored, the product of jam-making.

clue.text: Mount put a greater spurt on

indicators.note: the bigger word is put after the dash word

parts.note: a rush is a sudden spurt
more means greater

explanation.surface: Someone climbing speeds up towards the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb, but is the name of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota bears carved heads of four US presidents.

clue.text: Poet's alcohol-free retreat

parts.note: dry means without alcohol
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A writer's hideaway where no drink is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a seventeenth-century English poet laureate.
